commission: TRY FOREVER heartbeat 1500 repair after code-first review exposed a false monotonicity assumption.
head: feat/heartbeat-skill-lights-20260815

evidence.overlayUpdateReceiver: OverlayUpdateReceiver assigns heartbeat updatedMs from System.currentTimeMillis().
evidence.finding: Wall-clock milliseconds are presence/observation metadata, not a monotonic sequence. Treating an older positive updatedMs as a replay wound would reject legitimate heartbeats after clock correction and would exceed the proven contract. Equal millisecond timestamps can also occur across distinct broadcasts, so equality is not a unique persistence identity.

antagonism: Do not ship rollback or equal-timestamp collision rejection on top of System.currentTimeMillis().
Do not invent a new monotonic sequence/controller merely to save the first design; that would expand architecture and runtime ownership.
Keep the useful part: remove the duplicated 32768 literal by aliasing the projection ceiling to the existing OperatorState ingress constant.
Regression/art/doctrine must teach that byte count + SHA prove content identity while updatedMs currently proves only that an update timestamp was recorded and is positive.
Repair source before creating completion receipts; do not hide the abandoned first implementation.
revisedPlan: Repair HeartbeatPersistedEnvelopeProjection by removing the prior-update overload and all timestamp-order/collision semantics, retaining only positive timestamp presence plus exact byte/SHA integrity and the canonical ingress-size alias.

Replace the freshness regression source with contract fixtures proving the shared byte ceiling and that positive update timestamps are accepted independently of their absolute wall-clock value; no test may imply monotonic ordering.

Repair the warm-wall specimen so its seventh state is a clock-skew witness, not a rollback fault: self-consistent bytes/SHA with a positive timestamp may proceed to semantic ingestion; timestamp ordering earns no fault or motion by itself.
Record the wall-clock discovery in doctrine/evidence and leave accessibility dark unless a separate concrete defect is found.
